entries.name: ADHD
entries.use_for: Get several different solution ideas from isolated agents, then score and prune them.
entries.why: Isolated reasoning with no shared context during divergence, then a separate critic pass.
entries.summary: A skill that spawns several isolated reasoning runs under different cognitive frames, then runs a critic pass to score, cluster, prune weak ideas and deepen the best. It targets design decisions, naming, strategy and fuzzy debugging.
entries.best_for: Open-ended problems where you want options and named traps, not one quick answer.
entries.not_for: Costs more tokens than a single answer, and the gains shown come from the authors' own eval.

entries.name: AG Kit
entries.use_for: Install an Antigravity workspace with rules, skills, specialist agents, workflows and a safety hook.
entries.why: Bundles 20 roles, slash-command workflows, persistent memory and a destructive-command blocker.
entries.summary: A kit that installs a `.agents/` workspace contract for Google Antigravity: rules, skills, workflows such as /plan and /coordinate, 20 specialist roles, memory, MCP guidance and a hook that blocks dangerous commands. Python and Node validators check the setup.
entries.best_for: Antigravity users who want a ready agent workspace layout with guardrails.
entries.not_for: Only Antigravity is supported in production. Other tools may read the files but get no guarantee.

entries.name: Agent Skills (Addy Osmani)
entries.use_for: Add production-grade engineering skills (specs, TDD, review, CI, performance) to coding agents.
entries.why: Broad, well-structured engineering skill set; 107k stars and 93 contributors.
entries.summary: Collection of 25 engineering skills for AI coding agents covering the lifecycle: idea refinement, spec, planning, build, test/debug, review and ship. Installed with the open skills CLI (npx skills add) into 70+ agents, with slash commands like /spec, /plan, /review, /ship.
entries.best_for: Giving coding agents a structured, senior-engineer workflow with quality gates across spec, TDD, code review and shipping.
entries.not_for: Opinionated process skills, not tooling for a specific stack or product. Installing a single skill omits the repo-level references directory.

entries.name: AI-DLC Workflows
entries.use_for: Add a structured, auditable development workflow to Claude Code, Kiro, Codex, Cursor or Copilot.
entries.why: One harness-neutral core with phases, agents, human approval gates and an audit trail.
entries.summary: AI-DLC turns AI coding assistants into structured delivery workflows: 5 phases, 33 stages, 14 agents and 11 workflow profiles. It keeps state and an audit trail, and an aidlc CLI configures it per harness.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting a repeatable, reviewable process around AI-assisted software delivery.
entries.not_for: Quick ad-hoc coding; the process is heavy by design. The README warns to review generated output and costs.

entries.name: Automotive Engineering Suite
entries.use_for: Generate automotive engineering deliverables such as HARA, TARA, FMEA and AUTOSAR files with Claude skills.
entries.why: Every builder skill is paired with a reviewer skill that checks the output and produces a dashboard.
entries.summary: 152 Claude skills: 76 builders and 76 matching reviewers. They produce structured xlsx deliverables for ISO 26262, ISO/SAE 21434, SOTIF, AIAG-VDA quality, Automotive SPICE, communication protocols, diagnostics, AUTOSAR, calibration, MBSE and V&V.
entries.best_for: Automotive safety, security and quality engineers who want a consistent, reviewable draft of standards-based artifacts.
entries.not_for: Narrow to automotive. Output is AI-generated and must be reviewed by qualified engineers before use in a safety case.

entries.name: Builder.io Skills
entries.use_for: Add skills that collect feedback and errors and review or ship PRs under set policies.
entries.why: Separate policies for fixing, replying, reviewing, approving and merging.
entries.summary: A set of small agent skills, led by an experimental Factory skill. Factory turns feedback, telemetry and errors into policy-gated changes, with modules for collecting, babysitting PRs, reviewing queues and shipping.
entries.best_for: Teams who want agents to triage feedback and handle PR flow with explicit approval rules.
entries.not_for: Factory is marked experimental. It does not install integrations or create schedules for you.

entries.name: caveman
entries.use_for: Cut agent output tokens with terse caveman-style responses, commits and reviews
entries.why: Most-installed skill pack on skills.sh (~578k installs for the core skill) with commit/review/compress variants.
entries.summary: Caveman is an agent skill that makes AI coding agents answer in terse, compressed language and read less context, cutting input and output tokens while keeping code exact. It offers several levels (/caveman, /ultracave and more), plus Auto and Blocks modes, and reports benchmarks on Claude Code runs.
entries.best_for: Reducing token usage and cost of Claude Code or similar coding agents when you want short answers and less context read, without changing the code they produce.
entries.not_for: Users who want detailed, explanatory prose from their agent; the whole point is terse output. Not a general prompt-compression library for arbitrary LLM apps.

entries.name: Claude Autoresearch
entries.use_for: Have a coding agent iterate toward a measurable goal in a modify, verify, keep-or-revert loop.
entries.why: Generalizes Karpathy's autoresearch loop to any task with a metric, using git as memory.
entries.summary: A skill for Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex. You set a goal and a metric; the agent makes one change, commits, verifies, and keeps or reverts it, repeating. Twelve command files keep token use low.
entries.best_for: Optimizing anything with a number you can measure, such as tests, performance or content scores.
entries.not_for: Goals with no mechanical metric. Hook guardrails work in Claude Code only.

entries.name: Claude Code Skills & Plugins
entries.use_for: Pick from nearly 400 ready-made skills for engineering, marketing, compliance and more across 13 coding agents.
entries.why: Each skill bundles instructions, stdlib-only Python tools and reference docs, with converters for other agents.
entries.summary: A large library of skills, agents and personas, installable as Claude Code plugins or converted for Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and others. Skills cover engineering, DevOps, marketing, security, compliance, C-level advice and research. Python tools use only the standard library.
entries.best_for: Starting a skill collection quickly, or borrowing patterns for your own skills.
entries.not_for: Broad and uneven by nature; review each skill before trusting it. Some agents need a local sync step.

entries.name: Claude Skills (Fullstack Dev Skills)
entries.use_for: Install 67 developer skills for languages, frameworks, DevOps, security and testing in Claude Code.
entries.why: Skills activate on context and combine into workflows; includes a /common-ground command.
entries.summary: A Claude Code plugin marketplace with 67 skills in 12 categories. It adds nine workflow commands that manage epics through Jira and Confluence, and /common-ground to surface the agent's assumptions about your project.
entries.best_for: Full-stack developers who want a broad, ready skill set for Claude Code in one install.
entries.not_for: Narrow needs, or workflow commands without an Atlassian MCP server, which they require.

entries.name: CLI-Anything
entries.use_for: Generate or install command-line harnesses so AI agents can drive existing software.
entries.why: Comes with CLI-Hub, a registry of community-built agent-ready CLIs, plus a 7-phase generator.
entries.summary: CLI-Anything makes software usable by agents through structured CLIs with JSON output. You can install ready-made CLIs with cli-hub, or add the plugin and run the 7-phase generator to build a new harness for an app.
entries.best_for: You want agents to operate desktop or other software that has no agent-friendly interface.
entries.not_for: Quality depends on each generated or community CLI. It targets apps that can be wrapped by a command line.

entries.name: Comet
entries.use_for: Run long, resumable coding tasks through a requirements-to-archive workflow, and create, evaluate and release skills.
entries.why: Offers a Native workflow for strong models and a Classic OpenSpec plus Superpowers flow, with Pass@k skill scoring.
entries.summary: A resumable long-running task workflow and Skill platform for coding. It has two requirements workflows, Native and Classic, plus a toolchain to create, distribute and score skills with rubrics, Pass@k and Pass^k.
entries.best_for: Teams building and measuring their own agent skills and wanting governed phases from requirements to archive.
entries.not_for: A heavy process aimed at power users of coding agents. Native mode is meant for strong models.

entries.name: Compound Engineering
entries.use_for: Adopt a plan, work, review, compound loop for agentic engineering
entries.why: Every's widely used plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor; 108 contributors and a full brainstorm/plan/review skill set.
entries.summary: Plugin of 36 skills structuring agentic engineering as a loop: brainstorm, plan, build, review, then capture learnings so later work benefits. Runs on 14 agent hosts including Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting a repeatable plan-work-review workflow that records lessons in the repo for future agent runs.
entries.not_for: Process-heavy and opinionated; overkill for quick one-off edits. Invocation syntax differs per host.

entries.name: Conductor
entries.use_for: Make a coding agent write a spec and plan and get your review before it writes code.
entries.why: Keeps project context in the repo and has a git-aware revert for tracks, phases and tasks.
entries.summary: A plugin for agents like Antigravity and Claude Code that enforces a Context, Spec and Plan, then Implement lifecycle. Work is grouped into tracks, and project style and tech choices persist as shared context.
entries.best_for: Teams that want plan review and persistent project context for agent-written features and fixes.
entries.not_for: The README warns that it uses more tokens, especially on large projects. It adds process overhead for tiny changes.

entries.name: Context Hub
entries.use_for: Give coding agents current, versioned API docs through a CLI, so they stop inventing APIs.
entries.why: Open Markdown docs that you can inspect, with local agent notes and up/down feedback to authors.
entries.summary: Context Hub (chub) is a CLI that your coding agent uses to search and fetch curated, versioned, language-specific docs, such as OpenAI or Stripe APIs. Agents can add local annotations about gaps and vote docs up or down. All content is Markdown in the repo.
entries.best_for: Reducing API hallucinations in coding agents with up-to-date docs.
entries.not_for: Humans reading docs by hand. The README says it is designed for agents, and only API docs exist today, with skills on the roadmap.
keywords: up to date docs for coding agents

entries.name: Council of High Intelligence
entries.use_for: Run a panel of distinct analytical personas to debate a hard decision and return a verdict.
entries.why: Forces independent first positions, cross-examination and dissent, and labels claims as fact, inference or assumption.
entries.summary: A skill that assigns a hard question to different analytical personas, keeps their first views independent, makes them disagree, and returns a verdict with unresolved questions, kill criteria and a next step. It offers full, quick and duo modes across four agent tools.
entries.best_for: High-stakes or ambiguous choices where one reasoning path is not enough.
entries.not_for: Slow and token-heavy. The README says to skip it for simple facts or cheap, reversible decisions.

entries.name: Desloppify
entries.use_for: Give a coding agent a scan, score, review and fix loop to improve codebase quality over many sessions.
entries.why: Mixes mechanical detectors with LLM review, persists state across scans, and uses scoring built to resist gaming.
entries.summary: An agent harness that finds dead code, duplication and complexity, then adds LLM review of naming and module boundaries. It triages issues into a queue, has the agent fix them, rescans, and produces a score and badge. Covers 29 languages.
entries.best_for: Cleaning up a messy or AI-written codebase step by step with an agent.
entries.not_for: License is not clearly stated. It depends on an LLM agent doing the fixing, and full plugin depth is for only 8 languages.

entries.name: Everything Claude Code (ECC)
entries.use_for: Bundle skills, hooks, memory and security configs to tune an agent harness.
entries.why: Very widely starred harness configuration pack, actively maintained, MIT.
entries.summary: Agent harness optimization pack bundling 71 subagents, 311 skills, 97 commands, rules, hooks and install scripts. Guided manifest-driven setup for Claude Code, Codex and others, with doctor, repair and uninstall, plus a memory vault.
entries.best_for: Standing up a full, pre-configured agent environment with many skills, subagents and hooks at once.
entries.not_for: Very large footprint; adopting everything adds a lot of context and automation. The README warns to install only from official channels.

entries.name: Gentle-AI
entries.use_for: Set up memory, a workflow and review evidence for the AI coding agent you already use.
entries.why: One setup works across 17 agents, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode.
entries.summary: Gentle-AI configures coding agents with persistent memory, curated skills, MCP servers and a deterministic workflow. A binary tracks the valid next step and ties review evidence to the candidate change.
entries.best_for: Teams that use one or more coding agents and want shared memory, a fixed workflow and checkable review evidence.
entries.not_for: Not a standalone agent. It needs an existing agent such as Claude Code or Cursor. The README says its benchmarks are single runs (n=1).

entries.name: Godogen
entries.use_for: Have an agent build a game in Godot, Bevy, Babylon.js or three.js and prove it from the running game.
entries.why: Judges results from the running game or a recorded clip, not from a clean compile.
entries.summary: A generator that publishes into a fresh game repo, where Claude Code or Codex builds the game. It generates assets locally by default (images, 3D models, rigged characters, sound) and uses paid APIs for the rest. You can watch and steer or get a proof recording.
entries.best_for: Prototyping games with an agent across several engines.
entries.not_for: The repo is a generator, not a game. Some assets need paid APIs. Output quality depends on the agent.

entries.name: GSD Core
entries.use_for: Drive AI coding agents through a discuss, plan, execute, verify, ship loop that avoids context rot.
entries.why: Runs heavy work in fresh-context subagents so the main session stays lean.
entries.summary: A meta-prompting and spec-driven development system for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others. It installs with npx and repeats a five-step loop per phase, keeping state in files like STATE.md and CONTEXT.md.
entries.best_for: Larger projects where long AI sessions lose quality and you want a repeatable plan-and-verify process.
entries.not_for: Quick one-off edits. It adds a heavy process, and the README says the installer is required, so do not copy files by hand.

entries.name: gstack
entries.use_for: Add a set of slash commands that act as planner, reviewer and QA inside Claude Code.
entries.why: Packages one builder's whole Claude Code workflow as ready-to-run commands.
entries.summary: gstack is Garry Tan's Claude Code setup: opinionated tools that play roles like CEO, designer, engineering manager and QA. Commands include /office-hours, /plan-ceo-review, /review and /qa. Setup takes about 30 seconds.
entries.best_for: You want a ready-made, opinionated plan-review-QA workflow for Claude Code.
entries.not_for: It is one person's workflow, so expect opinions you may want to change. The README is long on personal story and productivity claims.

entries.name: HumanLayer Skills
entries.use_for: Install Claude Code skills for research-plan-implement flows, visual PRs, CLAUDE.md rewrites and agent loops.
entries.why: Practical workflow skills from HumanLayer, installed one at a time with npx skills.
entries.summary: A set of skills including rpi (research, design, then implement), design-control-loop, visual-pr, show-me, improve-claude-md, narrow-react-prop-types and build-iterated-agentic-loop. Each installs with npx skills add.
entries.best_for: Claude Code or Codex users who want structured research-then-implement workflows.
entries.not_for: Agents that do not read skills. The skills are tied to specific workflows, so read each one before adopting.

entries.name: i-have-adhd
entries.use_for: Make your coding agent answer action-first, with numbered steps and no filler.
entries.why: A short skill of 10 rules that you can fork and tune in one SKILL.md.
entries.summary: A skill that stops a coding assistant from burying the answer. Its 10 rules lead with the next action, number steps, cap lists at 5 items, give specific time estimates and drop preambles and closers. Fork SKILL.md to tune it.
entries.best_for: You want shorter, clearer, action-first responses from Claude Code or similar assistants.
entries.not_for: It only changes response style. It adds no tools or capabilities, and the rules are fixed unless you edit them.

entries.name: improve
entries.use_for: Have your best model audit a codebase and write plans that cheaper models execute.
entries.why: The skill never edits code; the self-contained plan is the product.
entries.summary: An agent skill with modes like quick, deep, security, perf, branch and next. It maps the repo, finds issues, rejects false ones with reasons, and writes numbered plan files with test and lint gates and STOP conditions. It can dispatch a cheaper executor and review the work.
entries.best_for: Cutting cost by splitting expensive thinking from cheap implementation.
entries.not_for: Direct code changes by the skill itself. It only plans, so you need another agent to implement.

entries.name: k-skill
entries.use_for: Give coding agents 125 skills for everyday Korean services such as KTX, buses, tax and shopping.
entries.why: Large Korea-specific skill set that installs with one npx command across many agents.
entries.summary: A collection of 125 agent skills grouped by area of Korean daily life, including rail timetables, bus booking, flights, travel safety and government services. Works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw. Some skills use a public proxy server.
entries.best_for: Developers and users in Korea who want agents to handle local services and lookups.
entries.not_for: Mostly useful only for Korean services, and the README is in Korean. Some skills are lookup-only and cannot book or pay.

entries.name: Loop Engineering
entries.use_for: Set up and score recurring agent loops (triage, PR babysitting, refactors) with ready patterns.
entries.why: A CLI to init, doctor and cost a loop, with a staged L1 report to L3 unattended rollout.
entries.summary: A pattern library and CLI for designing loops where agents find work, act, verify and persist state. Commands include init, doctor and cost. Works with Claude, Codex, Grok and Opencode, including thin GitHub Action loops.
entries.best_for: Teams moving from one-off prompting to scheduled, verified agent workflows around a codebase.
entries.not_for: One-shot rewrites. The README says it is a pattern library, not a rewrite the module button, and advises starting report-only.

entries.name: Loopy / Loop Library
entries.use_for: Find, adapt and design repeatable agent loops with built-in checks and stop rules.
entries.why: A public catalog of loops plus an installable skill that helps an agent audit, craft, run and publish them.
entries.summary: Two parts: a Loop Library website with published loops anyone can copy, and an optional Loopy skill that guides an agent to find, audit, repair, craft, run and save loops. A loop says what to do, how to check, and when to stop.
entries.best_for: Turning one-off agent prompts into repeatable workflows with feedback, such as fixing errors or raising test coverage.
entries.not_for: A catalog of prompt playbooks and a guide skill, not a runtime or agent framework. The skill relies on the live website catalog.

entries.name: Matt Pocock skills
entries.use_for: Opinionated engineering skills: codebase design, interface design, git guardrails and TDD workflows
entries.why: One of the most-installed community skill packs on skills.sh (several skills above 200k installs) from a well-known TS educator
entries.summary: Small, composable engineering skills for coding agents: grilling sessions (/grill-me), codebase and interface design, git guardrails and TDD workflows. Positioned as an alternative to process-owning frameworks like GSD, BMAD or Spec-Kit.
entries.best_for: Developers wanting lightweight, adaptable skills to fix misalignment and failure modes with agents.
entries.not_for: Opinionated to the author's workflow and TypeScript-leaning; not a full methodology or automation framework.

entries.name: mattpocock-skills-zh-CN
entries.use_for: Use Matt Pocock's engineering agent skills with Simplified Chinese instructions.
entries.why: Full Chinese translation of a popular small, editable skill set, keeping skill names and commands unchanged.
entries.summary: A Simplified Chinese localization of mattpocock/skills. Only natural-language text is translated; directory names, skill names, commands and code stay as they are. Install through the skills CLI or as a Claude Code plugin, then run the setup skill in each repo.
entries.best_for: Chinese-speaking developers, or teams working with Chinese-tuned models, who want those skills in their own language.
entries.not_for: A translated copy that tracks the upstream repo. Use the original if you work in English.

entries.name: pi-autoresearch
entries.use_for: Let the pi coding agent run autonomous benchmark-and-keep experiment loops on any metric.
entries.why: Splits a generic extension from per-domain skills, with session files that survive restarts.
entries.summary: An extension and skill for the pi terminal coding agent. It runs an optimization loop: try an idea, benchmark it, keep wins, revert regressions. Examples include test speed, bundle size and Lighthouse score. Progress lives in `.auto/log.jsonl` and a prompt file.
entries.best_for: Optimizing a measurable number, such as build time or bundle size, with an agent that works unattended.
entries.not_for: Works only inside the pi agent. You must have a command that yields a reliable metric.

entries.name: planning-with-files
entries.use_for: Keep long-running agent tasks on track with persistent markdown plan, findings and progress files.
entries.why: Simple, crash-proof planning pattern with broad adoption (~27k stars).
entries.summary: Planning skill that keeps task_plan.md, findings.md and progress.md on disk and uses lifecycle hooks to inject plan context each turn, so plans survive /clear, crashes and compaction. Installs across 60+ agents with native plugins for several.
entries.best_for: Long-running agent tasks that must not lose their plan across context resets.
entries.not_for: Tracks active execution state, not long-term fact memory (that is a different tool). Adds files and hooks to the project.

entries.name: ponytail
entries.use_for: Push your agent toward the smallest change: write less code, review and audit for bloat
entries.why: About 94k skills.sh installs for the core skill, plus review/audit/debt skills; 127 contributors.
entries.summary: Ponytail is an agent skill that pushes AI coding agents to write the minimal code a task needs. It reads the code a change touches first, then picks the simplest solution, leaves a small test for risky logic, and never cuts validation, error handling, security or accessibility. It marks deliberate shortcuts with comments that /ponytail-debt collects into a ledger.
entries.best_for: Teams using Claude Code or similar agents who want smaller diffs, lower token cost and fewer over-engineered abstractions, while still getting tests on branching or security-sensitive logic.
entries.not_for: Cases where you want the agent to build elaborate, general-purpose abstractions up front. It is a behavioural skill for agents, not a linter or code-size analysis tool.

entries.name: Prompt Master
entries.use_for: Have Claude write or fix prompts for any AI tool, from coding agents to image models.
entries.why: A fixed pipeline: detect the target tool, extract intent, ask at most three questions, then trim tokens.
entries.summary: Prompt Master is a Claude skill that writes prompts for other AI tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, Midjourney or Stable Diffusion. It detects the target tool, extracts nine dimensions of intent, asks up to three questions, applies safe techniques and returns one copyable prompt block.
entries.best_for: Getting a good first prompt for a coding agent or image model.
entries.not_for: Running tasks itself. It only writes prompts, and quality depends on the tool-specific guidance it carries.

entries.name: Qiushi Skill
entries.use_for: Add a set of problem-solving method skills so an agent investigates first and focuses on the main issue.
entries.why: Turns nine named methods into executable skills, plus a workflow layer to chain them.
entries.summary: A collection of AI agent skills built on classic dialectical and practice-based philosophy. It has one overall principle and nine method tools, such as contradiction analysis and investigation before judgment, plus a workflows layer that orders them.
entries.best_for: Users who want an agent to investigate before answering and review its own work.
entries.not_for: Methodology prompts, not code tooling. The README is in Chinese and the framing is political in origin.

entries.name: Qwen-MM-Plugins
entries.use_for: Adding native multimodal capabilities (vision, video, hardware control) to any coding-agent harness.
entries.why: Includes an omni-skill-creator that turns demonstration videos into reusable Agent Skills.
entries.summary: Qwen-MM-Plugins is a set of native multimodal plugins for Qwen models that make any agent harness multimodal-native. A guided installer wires the plugins into Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI and other harnesses, adding capabilities like 3D spatial reasoning, hardware operation, and video-to-skill conversion.
entries.best_for: Teams adding multimodal (image, video, hardware) capabilities to an existing agent harness without building plugins from scratch.
entries.not_for: Built around Qwen models specifically, so it may not suit a harness locked to a different model family.

entries.name: sanyuan-skills
entries.use_for: Install agent skills for code review, tutoring, skill auditing and knowledge-base building.
entries.why: Includes a senior-style code review skill covering SOLID, security, performance and error handling.
entries.summary: A collection of skills for Claude Code and other agent terminals. They include Code Review Expert, Sigma (a Socratic tutor), Skill Review, Skill Forge for creating skills, wiki-ingest and a guided book-study skill. Each installs with npx skills add and a path.
entries.best_for: You want a ready code-review skill or examples of well-structured skills to copy.
entries.not_for: A mixed bag, so check each skill before installing. Not a framework, only prompt-based skills.

entries.name: Superpowers
entries.use_for: Give a coding agent a disciplined workflow: brainstorming, planning, TDD, debugging and code review skills.
entries.why: One of the most installed skill packs on skills.sh (~395k installs for brainstorming); MIT.
entries.summary: Software development methodology for coding agents built from composable skills: brainstorming into a spec, a detailed implementation plan, then subagent-driven development with review, emphasizing red/green TDD, YAGNI and DRY. Skills trigger automatically.
entries.best_for: Structured, mostly autonomous multi-hour agent builds with design approval, planning and TDD.
entries.not_for: Heavy process; overkill for small edits. Opinionated about TDD and subagent workflow.

entries.name: superpowers-zh
entries.use_for: Install a Chinese translation of the superpowers skill set, plus four China-specific skills.
entries.why: Covers 26 coding tools, from Claude Code to Cursor, Gemini CLI and Qoder.
entries.summary: A Chinese community edition of the superpowers skill collection: translated workflow skills for brainstorming, TDD, debugging and code review, plus four original skills for Chinese development. It supports 26 AI coding tools and installs with npm.
entries.best_for: Chinese-speaking developers who want proven agent workflows in their own language.
entries.not_for: A translation of an upstream project. If you read English, use upstream superpowers directly. The README includes sponsor and course promotion.

entries.name: The Agency (agency-agents)
entries.use_for: Install a roster of specialist agent personas (design, engineering, marketing and more) into your coding agent.
entries.why: Each agent has a defined role, process and deliverables instead of a generic prompt.
entries.summary: A growing collection of specialist AI agent definitions grouped into divisions such as Design. Each has a personality, a process and expected deliverables. A companion desktop app installs the roster into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini and others.
entries.best_for: You want ready-made role-based sub-agents for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex rather than writing your own prompts.
entries.not_for: It is a set of prompt-style agent files, not a runtime or framework. Quality varies by agent, so review the ones you install.

entries.name: Universal Modder
entries.use_for: Let a coding agent research, mod and test almost any PC game you own.
entries.why: Covers recon, reverse engineering, fal-made art, 3D and audio, in-game testing and video.
entries.summary: A set of agent skills, tools and a shared knowledge base for modding PC games. The mod-any-game skill has playbooks for Unity, Unreal, Godot, .NET and many other engines. Other skills handle recon, research, reverse engineering and asset generation with fal.
entries.best_for: Modding games you own with an agent, including finding the engine and generating new assets.
entries.not_for: For games you own. Asset generation uses the fal service, and reverse engineering tools must be installed separately.

entries.name: unlazy
entries.use_for: Make an agent write acceptance checks first, run them, and only report what the evidence supports.
entries.why: A runnable gate checker that re-verifies finished work instead of trusting the agent's claim.
entries.summary: unlazy is a completion-discipline skill for large agent tasks. You write an acceptance ledger of checks, a Node script approves and runs them, and reverify re-runs gates already marked done. It adds a Depth Tree method for splitting work, plus orchestration and security guidance.
entries.best_for: Your agent stops early or claims it is done, and you want checks that run and can be audited.
entries.not_for: Gate CHECK lines are shell code, so you must read them before approving. Version 2.1.0 is unreleased source, so pin a commit. Overkill for small tasks.

entries.name: Waza
entries.use_for: Add eight small skills for engineering habits (think, debug to root cause, review, read sources) to your agent.
entries.why: Stays small on purpose, one job and one trigger per skill, built from real project failures.
entries.summary: Waza turns one engineer's habits into skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Each skill states the outcome, the red lines and how the result is verified, then lets the model pick the path. It also ships a minimal Claude Code statusline.
entries.best_for: Developers who want a light skill set, not a heavy framework.
entries.not_for: Opinionated and small by design. Not a full workflow framework like Superpowers or gstack.

entries.name: wshobson/agents
entries.use_for: Add a large marketplace of subagents, skills and commands across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more.
entries.why: Widely adopted multi-harness plugin marketplace with ~41k stars.
entries.summary: Large collection of plugins for AI coding tools: 94 plugins including 202 agents, 185 skills and 105 commands, sharing Markdown sources adapted to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot and others. Plugins cover Python, JS/TS, security, testing, infrastructure.
entries.best_for: Picking from a broad menu of specialist subagents and skills across languages and workflows.
entries.not_for: Huge catalog; installing indiscriminately bloats context. Quality varies by plugin and capabilities differ by harness.
